source.title: Suppression Is Not Forgetting: Residual Recoverability in Visual Concept Unlearning for VLMs
source.authors: Zhang-Yun Tan; Ze-Liang Zhang; Jia-Ni Liu; Susan Liang; Y. Y. Tang; Li-Sha Chen; Chen-Liang Xu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study's own visual-concept experiments show that suppression on one probe often leaves recognition or use available through other probes, refining the claim that apparent unlearning can be residual recoverability.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for prompt suppression, logit suppression, visual linear erasure, and parameter-update unlearning. Figure 1 values are not stated numerically in the text and are recorded as figure-only. Cited findings from other papers are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: New setting: off-the-shelf VLMs and visual concepts. The study applies prompt, decoding, representation-editing and five parameter-update unlearning methods. It then measures whether the concept stays recoverable through other query formats (MCQ, indirect) and whether forgetting holds across scorers and retraining runs. Its own numbers bear on A (does unlearning work) and E (recovery by re-querying).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that MMUnlearner is the only method whose short-answer reduction reliably exceeds its MCQ reduction. Add that GA and NPO rerun failures reflect generation collapse rather than selective forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates visual concepts in VLMs with prompt and decoding suppression, visual-token linear erasure, and parameter-update methods; it does not reproduce a single original unlearning-and-recovery recipe from the cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with probe format, prompt wording (soft versus hard target-list prompt), scoring rule, concept, intervention, and optimization run.
record.problems: The eligible concept counts are 13 for Qwen3-VL-2B, 10 for InternVL3-8B, and 14 for Qwen2-VL-7B. Figure 1 and Figure 2 contain results whose numerical values are not stated in the text. The parameter-update results are concept-dependent, and the paper reports sensitivity to scoring and training randomness.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result relevant to the claim was left out; 52 rows are included, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Text-only LLMs, hazardous knowledge (WMDP-style), RMU-type methods. Near-chance accuracy is never reached by any parametric method here.
No direction ablation restoring knowledge after unlearning; linear erasure is used only as the unlearning method. No mechanistic analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Jailbreaks, other languages, few-shot or in-context recovery attacks. Only alternative probe formats (MCQ, indirect) are tested.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Concept-level counts: GA and NPO show a positive LB drop on only 4/14 concepts, MMUnlearner on 7/14; all COCO object concepts nearly unchanged.
Cross-probe gap (ΔSA−ΔMCQ) with 95% CI. Only MMUnlearner's, 0.108 [0.018, 0.217], excludes zero.
Kate Winslet paired example: MMUnlearner misnames her in free form but selects her in MCQ; the advantage vanishes without the image.
Hard-prompt MCQ and indirect access, and logit suppression on Qwen3-VL-2B (said applied in Sec. 3.3). Shown only in Fig. 1, no rows.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's verdicts are revised as follows. C supports is removed: linear erasure is the unlearning intervention itself and lowers all probes, so it shows no recovery by internal edits. Hard-prompt rows are moved from E to A: the suppression prompt backfires, which is not a recovery attack. MCQ and indirect rows are relinked to E, since they measure recovery by alternative queries, and their states are set accordingly. Prompt and logit suppression are inference-time guardrails, not weight unlearning; treat their A links with that caveat. Rows r40–r49 compare scoring rules and largely duplicate Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests visual-concept access after several interventions, but does not test every unlearning method in the claim, nor whether every method reaches near-chance performance while preserving general ability.
No post-unlearning relearning or fine-tuning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.

It tests visual linear representation erasure and residual access through other probes, but does not ablate a single activation direction to restore the concept or directly establish a mechanistic account of blocking versus deletion.
It tests soft and hard suppression prompts and alternative probe formats, but not jailbreaks, other languages, or recovery using in-context information.
No new method is tested as a counter-method resisting the recovery attacks specified in the claim.

relation.reason: It reports its own results on whether suppression and unlearning remove the concept.

tranche.reason: New setting (off-the-shelf VLMs, visual concepts) with results on the claim. The reader's T5 is not needed, since the paper does not argue a version is wrong.

source_check.notes: Short paper, no appendix. Four VLMs: three for prompt/decoding/erasure, Qwen3-VL-8B for parameter updates. Erasure magnitudes and rerun values are figure-only. Concept counts come without means, and the Qwen2-VL-7B hard-prompt reversal covers only 6/14 concepts. 15 concepts, 10-14 eligible per model. Cross-probe gap CI excludes zero only for MMUnlearner.

statements.correction: Qwen3-VL-8B: exact-match drops GA 0.192 and NPO 0.210; semantic LB 0.040 for both (Table 2, Sec. 4.4).

Four VLMs: Qwen3-VL-2B, InternVL3-8B, Qwen2-VL-7B (prompt/decoding/erasure) and Qwen3-VL-8B (parameter updates). The MCQ result is from Qwen3-VL-8B only: target MCQ drop 0.000 (GA), 0.000 (NPO), 0.027 (MMUnlearner). Semantic SA LB drop: 0.040 (GA, NPO), 0.135 (MMUnlearner). The cross-probe gap CI excludes zero only for MMUnlearner [0.018, 0.217].
statements.problem: The MCQ numbers are right, but 'three VLMs' in the why field is wrong. The study uses four VLMs, and the cited MCQ result comes from one model only. 'Despite free-form reductions' is weak for GA/NPO (semantic LB 0.040).

statements.correction: Qwen3-VL-8B target MCQ access changes by 0.000-0.027 after GA, NPO or MMUnlearner (Table 1).

Qwen3-VL-8B target MCQ drop: 0.000 (GA, NPO), 0.027 (MMUnlearner). Semantic SA drop [LB, UB]: GA [0.040, 0.201], NPO [0.040, 0.215], MMUnlearner [0.135, 0.173]. Cross-probe gap 95% CI: GA [-0.025, 0.117], NPO [-0.025, 0.111], MMUnlearner [0.018, 0.217] (the only one above zero).
statements.problem: 'Free-form naming is suppressed' overstates GA and NPO. Their semantic SA LB drop is 0.040 and their cross-probe gap CIs include zero, so the study shows a reliable probe-form difference only for MMUnlearner.
